evidence.reason: `recorder.append(...)` is executed after `Popen(...)` but outside the `try` block that performs termination and waiting. If the record write raises (e.g. an OSError), `boot()` exits without stopping/reaping the spawned `systemd-run` child or closing the log, so the caller can release the run lock and clean up while the child is still pending. Moving the append into the existing `try` lets the current cleanup path terminate/wait the child on write failure. This is an ordinary robustness defect in existing intended cleanup behavior, not a new requirement.
